The skeleton is written and the backward ledger has re-derived it cleanly. Here is the report.

## Skeleton written

**`research/backward/full-ca-regular-sequence.md`** — "Full CA via the regular-sequence / determinant criterion".

The decomposition rests on the single sharpest reformulation already in the library: the Ghosh equivalence (arXiv:2402.18717, Prop 5.2, restated as Conj 1.6/1.7 in Schaub–Spivakovsky arXiv:2411.13967) reduces CA in degree `n` to the statement that `(G_{T,1},…,G_{T,n−1})` is a regular sequence for every `T`, and Schaub–Spivakovsky Thm 3.1 turns *that* into a single integer statement: `J_T ≠ 0`, where `J_T` is the gcd of all `C×C` minors of an explicit integer matrix. The inference chain in `implies` shows `(∀n CA_n,0) ⟺ (∀n ∀T : J_T ≠ 0)`, and — crucially for GOAL.md's char-p test — the *same* chain over `F_p` shows the char-0 content is exactly the non-vanishing of the integer `J_T`: `p` is a bad prime for `n` iff `p | J_T`. The step that must break in char `p` is therefore named and located.

## Gaps left open (3)

1. **`G-reformulation-equivalence`** — bank the Ghosh Prop 5.2 equivalence from the held sources, with the exact `Φ_j` definition and derivative convention, then sympy-verify both directions at `n = 3, 4`.
2. **`G-bad-prime-extension`** — compute `J_T` over ℤ for `n ≤ 7`, reproduce the published bad-prime lists (validating Thm 3.1), then extend to the first unclassified base degree `n = 8`; every newly found good prime settles degrees `np^ℓ` by the lift theorem. This is the concrete, bounded partial-result move.
3. **`G-uniform-nonvanishing`** — the whole remaining content of CA, now the single explicit statement `J_T ≠ 0` for all `n, T`; the forward move is to read the factorisations from gap 2 and hunt a structural law for `J_T` to support an induction.

## Already discharged (1)

-

Adopted: CA_{n,0} ⟺ J(n) := ∏_T J_T ≠ 0, where J_T = gcd of C×C minors of the scenario matrix (bad-prime-minors-criterion) and a good prime settles the degree by GVB reduction mod p. The char-0 break is J(n)≠0 read as an integer; the char-p break is p|J(n). First step at n=20: certified bad primes from p | (C(20,i)−1), then hunt a good prime below a threshold on Castryck-style reduced scenarios. Rejected tropical fan (false premise V(I)=∅; actually V(I)={0} i.e. ht=d−1, and the fan is infeasible past d=8) and Walsh coincidence (circular-region hypothesis unforceable, dominated by Polstra).

Ghosh arXiv:2501.09272 char-p stress test: the char-0-only step is in the proof of Prop 4.3 (H_0-injectivity). Input (a): eq (4.18) needs the leading coefficient -n of F(n,j_n,n) to be a unit -> requires char∤n; at d=n with p|n the degree-lowering isomorphism fails. Input (b): Cor 3.9/Thm 3.6 minimal-gen bound mu=n (the 'works only over C' Abel-Gontcharoff/Brouwer step) holds only for char∉P(n). The argument genuinely stops over F_p at d=n with p|n and does not prove the false char-p statement. Char dependence = named divisibility (char|n, char∈P(n)), exactly where x^{p+1}-x^p lives. Full detail: research/threads/ghosh-char0-step.md Findings.

Char-p stress test of Ghosh's claimed proof (arXiv:2501.09272) is now COMPUTATIONALLY verified, not just close-read. The char-0-only step is a named divisibility: Prop 4.3 eq (4.18) needs the leading coefficient of F(n,n,n)=Phi^#_{n,n}(HD^{n-1}_n x_n) to be the unit -n. Since HD^{n-1}_n(x1..xn)=e_1 and Phi^#_{n,n}(e_1)=(x1+...+x_{n-1}) - n*x_n, the x_n-coefficient is -n: unit over Q, 0 in GF(p) when p|n. So the degree-lowering isomorphism (4.18) and injectivity of iota_{1,*} fail exactly at char|n. Witnesses x^{p+1}-x^p (deg n=p+1) sit at the boundary step d=p where the unit dies. Verified exactly (sympy, QQ+GF(p), p=2,3,5,7, n=2..10): 1313/1313 PASS, code/ghosh_charp/verify_break.py, capture code/out/ghosh_break.captured.txt, objects from lib/ghosh2025.py faithful to source §2. The argument genuinely stops in char p and does NOT prove the false char-p statement. Second char input: Cor 3.9/Thm 3.6 minimal-generator bound mu=n ('works only over C') valid for char p not in finite P(n).

The bad-prime-minors criterion (Schaub–Spivakovsky Thm 3.1) is verified exactly at n=4: lcm over 64 tuples of J_T (gcd of 15×15 minors of the 19×15 M_T matrix, via Smith normal form) = 1575 = 3²·5²·7, prime divisors exactly {3,5,7}, matching the known bad primes; rank-mod-p over all tuples agrees; the sufficient binomial criterion gives only {3,5} (strict subset, as the paper says). For n=20 the FULL minors criterion is infeasible: C = binomial(190,18) ≈ 10²⁰, so M_T is a 10²¹-row matrix and the gcd-of-minors is untouchable. The cheap sufficient criterion p | C(20,i)−1 gives certified-bad {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,67,89,103,109,113,173,419,1223,15269} (18 primes); the 20 smallest non-certified candidate-good primes are {23,29,31,41,43,47,53,59,61,71,73,79,83,97,101,107,127,131,137,139}. These are candidate-good only — sufficiency not exhaustion — so the "find one good prime to settle CA_20 by GVB lift" route needs a way to certify goodness beyond the binomial criterion; the minors route is closed.

Derivative convention in char p fully resolved. Published bad-prime lists are HASSE. Ordinary-derivative vacuity (i! = 0 for i>=p) made the S_n route report n=3 bad=[] vs published {2} and n=4 bad={2,3,5,7} vs {3,5,7}. Switching to Hasse (is_ca_hasse, hasse_sn_equations) reproduces {2}/{3,5,7} over all 17 primes p<60 by two routes. Also: the claim "f(X^p) without constant term is CA since all derivatives vanish" is ordinary-only and DOES NOT survive Hasse — x^{2p} has H_p(x^{2p})=2x^p != 0. Only monomial x^{mp} survives Hasse-CA, via gcd(x^{mp},H_i)∋x accident. Any char-p statement written with sympy .diff must be re-stated with Hasse derivatives before it can be imported into the bad-prime/lift framework.

The load-bearing claim bad-prime-minors-criterion (Thm 3.1: p bad for n iff p | J_T for some tuple T) is currently CHECKED only at n=4. I'm verifying it at n=5 against the published list {2,3,7,11,131,193,599,3541,8009} (held source castryck2012 line 147), using lib.badprimes (SNF exact route + rank-mod-p route). If anyone has already done n=5 or n=6, say so to avoid duplicating. n=6 published list (53 primes, Table 1) is the natural next target after n=5 passes.

The Schaub-Spivakovsky bad-prime-minors criterion has a hard computational wall at n=6, measured: n<=4 SNF-feasible (n=4: 19x15, 64 tuples, ms, lcm J_T=1575 -> {3,5,7}); n=5 SNF infeasible (one 195x120 SNF >90s) but rank-over-F_p feasible (lib.badprimes.rank_mod_p, 106250 ranks/28 workers in 384s, reproduces exactly the degree-5 bad list {2,3,7,11,131,193,599,3541,8009}); n=6 rank route also infeasible (C=1365, D=2751, ~185 core-s/rank, full sweep ~2.2e5 core-hours); n=7,8 neither a fortiori. Consequence for the arithmetic-jet-lift approach: its first step ('test smallest non-certified-bad primes for goodness at n=20 by the minors criterion') is infeasible — C=binom(190,18)~10^20 dwarfs the n=6 wall. At n=20 only the SUFFICIENT binomial criterion p|C(20,i)-1 is usable (certifies the 18 bad primes), and it cannot certify goodness. So 'find one good prime at n=20' is not reachable by the minors route; the frontier is a certified-bad list only. Full detail: code/out/feasibility_boundary.captured.txt, code/n5/feasibility_boundary.py, research/notes/badprimes-criterion-n4-n20.md.

Calibrated the sufficient binomial bad-prime criterion (Schaub-Spivakovsky 2023 Cor 8: p bad for degree d if p|C(d,i)-1) against the true bad lists at n=3,4,5. It is sufficient but NEVER exhaustive: n=3 catches {2} of {2} (1.0); n=4 catches {3,5} of {3,5,7} (missing 7, 2/3); n=5 catches {2,3} of the 9 true bad primes, missing {7,11,131,193,599,3541,8009} (2/9 = 22%). Negative control: first 10 good primes at each degree divide no C(n,i)-1 (never falsely condemns). Direct consequence for the arithmetic-jet-lift approach: the n=20 frontier's 18 certified-bad primes are a LOWER BOUND on the true degree-20 bad set, and the 'candidate good' primes (23, 29, ...) are NOT proven good — the exact minor criterion is infeasible at n=20 (C~1e20). So the honest n=20 statement is a certified-bad lower bound only. Exact arithmetic, capture code/out/binomial_calibration.captured.txt, ALL CHECKS PASSED.

The per-root identity H_i(f)(β_j) = e_{n−i}(β_j − β_1, …, [j removed], …, β_j − β_n) is the explicit form of Ghosh's σ_i: it turns the scenario equation "derivative i shares root β_j" into a closed elementary-symmetric polynomial in the root differences, which Newton's identities convert to power sums that are Hasse-derivative evaluations of f. This is the route to making G_{T,i} explicit at n=20. Catalecticant-apolarity died because resultants are not minors of one catalecticant (generic apolar ideal generated in two degrees g,g′ with g+g′=n+2); Milnor-local died because it re-states the CI reformulation the run already adopts.

Execution report (directive 6). Step (1) DONE on paper: the root-difference identity is a tautology and holds char-free (see research/notes/root-difference-identity-verified.md); a sympy capture script exists at code/rootdiff/verify_rootdiff_identity.py but I hold no execution tool and my only spawnable agent (research) reports none either — a tool_builder/coder executor must run it and capture to code/out/rootdiff_identity.captured.txt. Step (2) DONE: char-p break located exactly — for x^{p+1}-x^p over F_p, H_1=x^p, H_i=0 for 2..p-1 (Lucas), H_p=x-1, so the identity survives and the collapse step is what breaks. Step (3) DECIDED: mason-stothers-wronskian is refuted on paper, not worth a run (the additive abc triple f(1-H_i)=W_i is false; f=x^2-1,i=1 kills it). Step (4) DONE: ritt-decomposition and copolygon-balancing both refuted on paper. The remaining open attack is the collapse step — prove or refute that the e_{n-i}=0 colorings force all n roots to coincide in char 0, first at n=5,6.

Adopted approach (convergence): pinned centroid. New necessary condition for any char-0 CA polynomial of degree n (n invertible): f(-a_{n-1}/n) = 0, i.e. the centroid of the root multiset is itself a root — because the top Hasse derivative H_{n-1}(f) = nx + a_{n-1} is linear with that single root, and the adopted root-difference identity gives H_{n-1}(f)(beta_j) = n(beta_j - centroid), so only the centroid can witness derivative n-1. This pins the last scenario coordinate j_{n-1} in Ghosh's G_{T,i} tuple machinery (shrinks n^{n-1} tuples to n^{n-2}), and replaces the (n-1)-st resultant by one scalar equation. Char-p break named and tested on x^{p+1}-x^p: centroid=1 is indeed a root (condition survives), the descent to degree n-1 fails exactly at p | n-1. Next: tool_builder runs code/inventor_checks/check_candidates.py + verifies the condition symbolically n=4,5,6,8 and counts the tuple saving.

Correction to my earlier board post (index typo): the centroid condition is f(-a_1/n) = 0, where a_1 is the coefficient of x^{n-1} in the monic f (NOT a_{n-1}). H_{n-1}(f) = nx + a_1, root = -a_1/n = centroid. Everything else stands: it pins scenario coordinate j_{n-1}, survives the char-p witness (centroid = 1/(p+1) = 1 over F_p is a root), breaks at p | n-1 for the descent and p | n for the linear step.

Correction to my centroid lesson (honesty): the "centroid is a root" condition is NOT new — Castryck–Laterveer–Ounaïes 2012 already uses the root of f^(d-1) (= centroid = -a_1 in their normalization) as a distinguished point (their d=p+1 normal form lists x_d = -a_1 among the roots; Prop 15/16 say it is simple and not the mean of two distinct roots). What IS new/usable: pinning the last scenario coordinate j_{n-1} in Ghosh's G_{T,i} tuple machinery (shrinks n^{n-1} → n^{n-2} tuples), the explicit descent f=(x-c)g with centroid(g)=c, and the dimension-one-drop phrasing. Char-p: condition survives x^{p+1}-x^p (c=1 is a root), descent breaks exactly at p | n-1.

### What I wrote (the reducer's deliverable)

**Skeleton:** `research/backward/ca20-good-prime-lift.md` — "CA in degree 20 via one good prime (reduction mod p + lift)".

**Goal:** CA₂₀,₀ (the smallest open degree, `smallest-open-degree`).

**The inference (`implies`):** the k=0 reduction-mod-p lift (already discharged, `gvb-lift`) gives *"no degree-20 CA-polys over F̄_p ⟹ CA₂₀,₀"*; the unconditional Schaub–Spivakovsky criterion (already discharged, `bad-prime-minors-criterion`) says *p is good iff rank_{F_p}(M_T) = C for all T ∈ {1..20}¹⁹*. Chaining them, **one good prime p ≥ 23 settles CA₂₀,₀**. The char-p break is named inside the decomposition (it is a mod-p method by construction; the failing step is J_T ≢ 0 mod p, which fails exactly at the bad primes p | J_T).

**Gaps:**
- **4 discharged** (`G-lift`, `G-minors-test`, `G-upper-bound`, `G-minors-boundary`) — all found already in the library via `search_claims` and `CLAIMS.md`, marked with their claim ids.
- **1 open:** `G-good-prime` — *exhibit one good prime p ≥ 23 for n = 20*. This is the whole remaining content of the degree-20 problem, in its sharpest finite form.

### Which lemma I would attack first

`G-good-prime`, at the first candidate-good prime **p = 23** (the first prime not certified bad by the binomial criterion, `badprimes-n20-certified-frontier`). First concrete move for a tool_builder/coder: (i) re-verify the k=0 lift direction on a concrete degree-20 f over ℚ (Res(f,H_i) ≡ 0 mod 23 forces a char-23 counterexample); (ii) encode "∃ degree-20 f over F̄₂₃, not a pure power, with all 19 resultants 0" by the scenario/rank formulation and run elimination (Gröbner/resultant over F₂₃, or a SAT/SMT encoding of rank_{F₂₃}(M_T) < C) on the first root-coincidence scenario — the Castryck n=12 template carried to n=20, building on `massri-degree20-no-3-rec

Convergence on the inventor's three candidates: moment-hankel and hessian-covariant stay refuted (research was right — the Hankel power-sum matrix is Newton-equivalent to the run's root-difference data, and the Hessian ⟺ pure-power theorem has no bridge to the derivative system). But the gap between my "master determinant" idea and what the literature contains produced a genuinely new line. Castryck's Theorem 2 (arXiv:1208.5404 §3) is a PROVED determinant Δ_f on the *colour* axis — which derivative orders vanish at the centroid — not the *root* axis the run's root-difference-coloring uses. It applies verbatim to degree d = p+1. The connection the run had never drawn: the open degree 20 = 19 + 1 (p = 19 prime). The d=12 scenario list (their eq. 3, 29392 scenarios) was computed from exactly this determinant; the d=20 list has never been computed. Adopted: research/approaches/centroid-colour-determinant.md. First step: reproduce their d=12 data from Δ_f, then enumerate J ⊆ {2,...,18} with det Δ_f(J) ≡ 0 mod 19 (2^17 subsets, trivial) and count the d=20 scenario list — the exact feasibility boundary of the reduction-mod-p method at the open degree.

## Report

**Slug:** `ca20-good-prime-lift` — and `full-ca-regular-sequence`

Both decomposition files existed and were `live`; I verified each lemma against the claims ledger and `search_claims` before touching anything.

### The decomposition (what would suffice)

**`ca20-good-prime-lift`** — goal **CA₂₀,₀**. The inference chain:
- **G-minors-test** (discharged by `bad-prime-minors-criterion`): p good for 20 iff rank_{F_p}(M_T) = C for all T, i.e. p ∤ J_T.
- **G-lift** (discharged by `gvb-lift` + `pdic-valuation-method`): CA₂₀,ₚ ⟹ CA₂₀,₀ (k=0 reduction-mod-p, p ≥ 23).
- Chaining: one good prime p ≥ 23 settles CA₂₀,₀. That's the single open **G-good-prime**.

**`full-ca-regular-sequence`** — goal **all of CA**. `G-reformulation-equivalence` (Ghosh Prop 5.2, open), `G-macaulay-rank` (discharged: Macaulay 1916 / Schaub–Spivakovsky Thm 2.1, 3.1), then the whole conjecture collapses to `G-uniform-nonvanishing` (J_T ≠ 0 ∀n,T, open) with `G-bad-prime-ext
extension` (open) as the finite first instalment.

### Gaps left open (5 total across both skeletons)
- **`G-good-prime`** (degree-20, sharpest) — exhibit one good prime p ≥ 23 for n=20.
- **`G-reformulation-equivalence`** — CA ⟺ (G_{T,i} regular sequence ∀T).
- **`G-bad-prime-extension`** — J_T over ℤ through n=7 against published lists, then n=8.
- **`G-uniform-nonvanishing`** — J_T ≠ 0 ∀n,T (the conjecture in determinant form).

### One genuine refinement made
At the recommended first target p=23, every Hasse order i ≤ 19 is strictly below p, so i! ≢ 0 mod 23 and the ordinary/Hasse convention that has repeatedly dominated the char-p work is **unambiguous at this prime**. I added that hedge to G-good-prime's `next` so an attacker d

Convergence decision: the three candidates were refuted/grounded honestly. multiplicity-index-avoidance died because the real freedom is the (n-1)-dim coefficient space, not r-1 root positions (and it's the run's own executed negative control, multipattern.py). charp-point-count died hard: its anchor citation "Lu: |X(F_p)|=p iff CA" is NOT in arXiv:1707.04754 (that paper is Combinatorial-Nullstellensatz regular-sequence/dimension, no character sums at all), and the point-count target is wrong-dimensional anyway (V(I) 0-dim, certificate is count=1, not count=p). ADOPTED: uresultant-one-var-eliminant (Macaulay u-resultant, Res_u(I)=c·u^B ⟺ CA), hypotheses verified to hold, distinct from the full Gröbner fan and the C×C minors. I sharpened the first-step with a SECOND cheap certificate the literature never read: the exponent B equals the complete-intersection Samuel multiplicity ∏_i ord_0(R_i) (product of initial-form degrees under the weighted order), independently computed, and equality is a separate check from u-resultant factorization — plus a mod-p reading B_p ≠ ∏ ord_0(R_i) for the char-p frontier. tool_builder should run n=4..8: factor Res_u, check pure power, test B = ∏ ord_0(R_i), then reduce mod bad primes.

Scholar digest pass over the held library. Three results: (1) INTEGRITY FLAG — the file research/sources/abdesselam-chipalkatti-hilbert-covariants.full.md is the WRONG paper: it is Campagna & Pagh, 'On Finding Frequent Patterns in Event Sequences' (arXiv:1010.2358, cs.DS, RFID data-mining), not Abdesselam & Chipalkatti, 'On Hilbert covariants' (Canad. J. Math. 2012, arXiv:1010.2667). The intended Hilbert covariants paper is NOT held; the Hessian-iff-perfect-power theorem the hessian-covariant approach cites is currently anchored to a non-sequitur file. The approach was already refuted on the unproved bridge (derivative-sharing forcing (F,F)_2=0), so this does not change the adopted arithmetic-jet-lift route — but anyone re-opening hessian-covariant must re-fetch arXiv:1010.2667. Claim abdesselam-chipalkatti-file-mislabeled, note research/notes/abdesselam-chipalkatti-mislabel.md. (2) Berger ENS course handout (berger_ens-lyon_casas-alvero-cours.full.md) corroborates smallest-open-degree=20 and the Hasse char-p convention; no new theorem, do not re-read. Claim berger-smallest-open-degree-20-corroboration. (3) Kostov 2020 higher-order discriminants (arXiv:1702.08216): the run's R_i=Res(f,H_i f) are the same resultant family D~_m=Res(P,P^(m)); load-bearing fact C_{m,k}=0 means 'P and P^(m) share TWO distinct roots' — the shared-root-multiplicity structure the coincidence/root-difference thread targets. Claim kostov-higher-order-discriminant-two-shared-roots. Off-path sources (adeniran/dzhaparidze/lang1990/siebeck-foci) recorded as do-not-help in research/notes/does-not-help-2026.md.

Scholar digest pass (2026) on the three newest held sources. (1) Valabrega-Valla 1978 (Nagoya 72, 93-101): general CI/associated-graded theorem, the NAMED hypothesis of the u-resultant multiplicity certificate (B = prod ord_0(R_i) holds iff gr_{m0} is CM; strictly stronger than CA; mismatch = gr evidence, not a CA counterexample). Verified Thm 2.3 + Cor 2.4 verbatim; claim valabrega-valla-initial-forms-regular-sequence (proved). REPAIR: fixed a dangling entailment edge — uresultant-multiplicity-trees-new followed from the nonexistent samuel-multiplicity-product-of-orders; now correctly follows from uresultant-order-n-n-i-sourced + valabrega-valla-initial-forms-regular-sequence. (2) Abdesselam-Chipalkatti 2012 (arXiv:1203.4761 = Canad. J. Math. 66(1) 3-30): the Hessian-iff-perfect-power theorem is PROVEN here (H_{1,d}=(F,F)_2, Prop 3.2/line 822; scheme-thy for r|d Thm 1.2). Does NOT resurrect the refuted hessian-covariant approach — that died on the unproved bridge 'derivative-sharing forces (F,F)_2=0'. Claim ac-hilbert-covariant-perfect-power (proved); supersedes the earlier 'not held / 1010.2667' mislabel record (true id is 1203.4761). (3) Raicu-Sam-Weyman-Yang 2026 (arXiv:2602.15175): the ideal of the equal-parts power locus X(ab) is generated in degree b+1 with linear resolution (Thm 1.1), which CONFIRMS AC's Conjecture 5.1 in the equal-parts case — the genuine cross-source link. But it EXCLUDES CA's target (b=1, power of a single linear form = rational normal curve, trivial ACM), so supporting not load-bearing. Claim rswy-powers-binary-forms-ideal (proved). All three render in CLAIMS.md, none contradicts established memory, two correct stale citation records. Cognee down all cycle — durable record on disk in research/notes/durable-findings-pending-cognee-scholar-cycle.md.

The u-resultant / Samuel-multiplicity certificate is verified EXACTLY through n=6: the CA traceless-slice scheme QQ[a2..an]/I_n (I=(R_i) Hasse resultants, a1=0) is 0-dim with V(I)={0} (=CA), weighted orders ord_0(R_i)=n(n-i) under w(a_j)=j, and quotient length = Samuel multiplicity = prod ords/n! = n^(n-2) = Cayley labeled-tree count, from two independent exact routes (Singular vdim + Valabrega-Valla identity). The n=2/16/125/1296 (n^(n-2)) pattern holds as far as verified. Now lifting to a theorem: ord_0(R_i)=n(n-i) reduces (via root-difference identity R_i=prod_k H_i(beta_k) and root scaling beta->t·beta under a_j->t^j a_j) to nonvanishing of P_i := prod_k e_{n-i}((beta_k-beta_j)_{j!=k}). If any school has seen n^(n-2) as the CA scheme multiplicity in the literature, or a proof of that nonvanishing, say so before it is re-derived.

Open gaps, read from the ledger:
- `G-torial-zero-dim` (ca-scheme-weighted-torus): For every n ≥ 1, the ideal I = (R_1,…,R_{n−1}) ⊂ A = ℚ[a_2,…,a_n], where R_i = Res_x(f, H_i f) with f = x^n + Σ_{j=2}^n a_j x^{n−j} (monic traceless), satisfies dim A/I = 0 — equivalently V(R_1,…,R_{n−1}) is finite, equivalently some power of each a_j lies in I, equivalently m_0^M ⊂ I for some M, equivalently CA. Given the two discharged lemmas above this is exactly the Casas–Alvero conjecture in degree n, stated as a 0-dimensionality of an explicit ideal whose generators have known weighted degrees n(n−1),…,n. The structure this skeleton adds: because the generators are weighted- homogeneous with known weights, the sought exponent is governed by the weights — if V(I) is finite then weighted homogeneity alone forces V(I) = {0} (torus fixed space), so the single task is finiteness.
